title: Fix token limit: exclude cache tokens from cumulative input cost cap
description:
## Context
Sessions are hitting the 500K input token limit after only ~6 tool calls because the accumulation counts cache_read_input_tokens and cache_creation_input_tokens at full weight. These cache tokens are NOT billed at full rate (cache_read is 90% cheaper, cache_creation is 25% more), so including them massively inflates the count. A short triage session with an Explore agent hits 107% after just a few turns.

## What to Change
- **packages/server/src/services/session-runner.ts line 554**: Change from:
  \`managed.inputTokens += inputTokens + cacheCreation + cacheRead\`
  To:
  \`managed.inputTokens += inputTokens\`
  Only count \`input_tokens\` (the non-cached portion) toward the cumulative cost cap. Cache tokens (cache_read, cache_creation) should be excluded since they don't represent full-cost API usage.

- **Also consider increasing DEFAULT_LIMITS.maxInputTokens** (line 40) from 500_000 to something higher (e.g., 2_000_000) since even without cache, cumulative input across many turns adds up fast.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] managed.inputTokens only accumulates input_tokens (not cache_creation or cache_read)
- [ ] A session with ~10 turns and moderate context does NOT hit the 500K limit prematurely
- [ ] Token usage warning and stop messages still show accurate percentages
- [ ] The context % display (line 549-551) can still include cache tokens for UX (shows actual context window usage per turn) — this is separate from the cost cap

## Technical Notes
- session-runner.ts line 545-554: the usage extraction and accumulation logic
- input_tokens from Anthropic API = non-cached input tokens (the billable portion)
- cache_creation_input_tokens = tokens written to cache (billed at 1.25x but only on creation)
- cache_read_input_tokens = tokens read from cache (billed at 0.1x)
- The contextSize=200000 and usedPercentage on lines 549-551 is for the per-turn context display — keep that as-is, it's correct for showing context window usage
- Default limit of 500K may still be too low even without cache — user can adjust via project settings (max_session_input_tokens)
close_reason: Fixed: only count non-cached input_tokens toward cost cap. Raised default limits to 2M/500K/500.

title: Fix: session API calls fail with Project ID required
description:
## Context
Sending messages, resuming, cancelling sessions all fail with "Project ID required". The sessions router has requireProjectMember middleware which needs :projectId, but the client calls session-scoped URLs (/sessions/:id/resume) without a project prefix.

## Root Cause
Server mounts the same router at two paths:
- /api/projects/:projectId/sessions — project-scoped (has projectId)
- /api/sessions — session-scoped (no projectId)

The router internally uses router.use(requireProjectMember) which needs projectId on ALL routes, but session-scoped operations (get, cancel, resume, answer, events) are called via /api/sessions/:id/... where projectId is undefined.

Client resources.ts calls:
- resume: /sessions/${sessionId}/resume (no projectId)
- cancel: /sessions/${sessionId}/cancel (no projectId)
- answer: /sessions/${sessionId}/answer (no projectId)
- get: /sessions/${sessionId} (no projectId)
- events: /sessions/${sessionId}/events (no projectId)

## What to Change

### Option A (preferred — client fix):
- packages/client/src/lib/resources.ts: Change all session-scoped API methods to use project-scoped URLs: /projects/${projectId}/sessions/${sessionId}/...
- Update method signatures to accept projectId parameter
- packages/client/src/hooks/use-sessions.ts: Pass projectId (from useProject()) to all session API calls

### Option B (server fix):
- Split sessions router into project-scoped and session-scoped routers
- Session-scoped router: no requireProjectMember, look up project from session record
- More work but cleaner API design

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Resume session works without "Project ID required" error

title: Implement ClaudeConfigService — filesystem CRUD with mtime conflict detection
description:
## Project Context
Agent sessions discover skills, agents, commands, and CLAUDE.md from .claude/ directories on the filesystem. The web UI needs to read/write these files. This service is the foundation — all routes and UI depend on it.

## Reasoning
Chose direct filesystem CRUD over DB storage because the Agent SDK only reads from disk. Storing in DB would create sync issues (same problem we had with Beads). Optimistic mtime concurrency chosen over file locking because conflicts are rare (small trusted team) and mtime is simpler.

## What to Change
- **New file**: packages/server/src/services/claude-config-service.ts

### ClaudeConfigService class
Constructor takes basePath (project_root or repo.path). All operations scoped to \${basePath}/.claude/.

Methods:
- getClaudeMd(): { content: string; mtime: number } | null
- putClaudeMd(content, expectedMtime?): void — throws ConflictError if mtime mismatch
- listSkills(): SkillSummary[] — reads .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md, parses YAML frontmatter for name/description/triggers
- getSkill(name): { content: string; mtime: number }
- putSkill(name, content, expectedMtime?): void — creates .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md
- deleteSkill(name): void — removes .claude/skills/<name>/ directory
- listAgents(): AgentSummary[] — reads .claude/agents/*.md, parses frontmatter
- getAgent(name), putAgent(name, content, expectedMtime?), deleteAgent(name)
- listCommands(), getCommand(), putCommand(), deleteCommand() — same pattern for .claude/commands/*.md
- listRules(), getRule(), putRule(), deleteRule() — same pattern for .claude/rules/*.md
- getSettings(): object | null — read-only, parses .claude/settings.json

### Conflict detection
On PUT, if expectedMtime is provided:
1. stat() the file, compare Math.floor(stat.mtimeMs) with expectedMtime
2. If mismatch: throw ConflictError with { currentContent, currentMtime }
3. Routes catch ConflictError → 409 response with current file content

### Frontmatter parsing
Skills use YAML frontmatter (--- delimited). Parse with a simple regex or yaml library (check if js-yaml is already a dependency). Extract: name, description, triggers, domain, role.
Agents use markdown frontmatter with: name, description, model.

### Path safety
Validate name param to prevent directory traversal:
- Must match /^[a-z0-9-]+$/ (kebab-case only)
- No .., no /, no absolute paths
- Throw 400 if invalid

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All CRUD methods work for skills, agents, commands, rules, CLAUDE.md
- [ ] Optimistic mtime conflict detection throws ConflictError on stale writes
- [ ] Frontmatter parsed correctly for skills (YAML) and agents (markdown)
- [ ] Path traversal prevented (only kebab-case names allowed)
- [ ] Returns null/empty for non-existent .claude/ directory (graceful degradation)
- [ ] Unit tests: CRUD operations, conflict detection, frontmatter parsing, path validation

## Technical Notes
- Use fs.readFileSync/writeFileSync/mkdirSync/rmSync (sync is fine — small files, infrequent operations)
- Skill file layout: .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (directory per skill)
- Agent/command/rule layout: .claude/<type>/<name>.md (flat files)
- CLAUDE.md is at .claude/CLAUDE.md (not root CLAUDE.md — that's the repo's own file)
- Wait — actually CLAUDE.md lives at the repo root, not inside .claude/. Check both locations.
- Existing pattern: BeadsService in services/ wraps CLI; this wraps filesystem instead

title: Background Triage Sessions: Async Processing + Archive Cleanup
description:
## Context

Currently, triage sessions timeout after ~120s and are marked as completed after ~200s. This blocks long-running triage operations (processing many captures, complex analysis) and prevents users from interacting with the session or resuming work.

Users need:
1. Triage sessions to continue running in the background without artificial timeouts
2. Sessions remain visible in the UI for transparency and interaction (send follow-up messages)
3. Idle sessions automatically cleanup after 1 day to prevent database bloat
4. Notifications for key events: questions (needs input), completion, and errors/blockers

## What to Change

**Session Lifecycle:**
- Remove timeout logic that forces sessions to 'completed' state
- Keep sessions in 'running' or 'idle' state indefinitely until user explicitly completes or deletes
- Allow sessions to stay managed for resumption even after long idle periods

**Notification System:**
- Emit 'session:question' event → notification badge/toast in UI
- Emit 'session:completed' event → notification when triage finishes
- Emit 'session:error' event → alert user on failures/blockers

**Cleanup Service:**
- Create async job to scan for idle sessions (status='idle', last activity >24hrs ago)
- Move old sessions to new 'archived_sessions' table (preserves history, unclutters active list)
- Track archive_date in archived_sessions for audit trail
- Run cleanup daily (configurable via env: SESSION_IDLE_TTL_HOURS, default 24)

**Database:**
- Create new 'archived_sessions' table (schema mirrors sessions table)
- Add migration to move old idle sessions
- Optional: add 'is_archived' flag to sessions table instead of separate table (simpler, choose approach with user)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Long-running triage sessions do NOT timeout or mark as completed automatically
- [ ] Sessions remain visible in UI and user can send messages anytime
- [ ] User receives notifications for: questions asked, session completed, errors/blockers
- [ ] Idle sessions (no activity >24hrs) automatically moved to archive
- [ ] Archived sessions queryable in history but hidden from active session list
- [ ] Cleanup runs daily without blocking main server
- [ ] SESSION_IDLE_TTL_HOURS env var configurable (defaults to 24)
- [ ] Integration tests verify: session stays 'idle' indefinitely, cleanup works, resume works

## Technical Notes
- Session timeout is currently in SessionRunner (~120s implied by capture context)
- Current session states: queued, running, waiting_input, idle, validation_failed, completed, failed, cancelled, detached
- Socket.IO rooms: 'session:<sessionId>' for session-specific events
- No timeout in agent SDK itself — timeout is likely in HTTP client or server-side polling
- Cleanup job should use scheduler (PM2 cluster mode compatible) or Node interval with graceful shutdown
- Consider: use existing 'detached' state for old idle sessions before archiving? Or create new state? Recommend archiving instead (cleaner).

Wired cleanup into server lifecycle with graceful shutdown.

## Context
When the triage agent session runs, it discovers auth configuration at runtime by echoing env vars (CTW_API_KEY, ADMIN_API_KEY) and making curl commands with Bearer tokens visible in the stream. - [ ] Stream view redacts or masks any accidentally leaked sensitive values (defense in depth)

title: Fix: sessions stuck in Queued — no agent runner to execute them
description:
## Context
When creating a new agent session, it gets status 'queued' but never transitions to 'running'. The UI shows "1 active, max 3 concurrent" indicating capacity is available, but the session stays queued. There is no agent runner/worker process that picks up queued sessions and starts Claude Code via the Agent SDK.

## Root Cause
The POST /sessions endpoint creates sessions with status='queued' but no background process exists to:
1. Poll for queued sessions
2. Start Claude Code via @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk query()
3. Stream events back and update session status to 'running'
4. Handle completion/failure and update status

The playgrounds/agents/ has a working reference for the Agent SDK integration, but the server has no equivalent session runner.

## What to Change

### packages/server/src/services/session-runner.ts — New service
- Poll or subscribe for sessions with status='queued'
- For each queued session:
  1. Update status to 'running'
  2. Start Agent SDK query() with session.prompt, session.model, AbortController
  3. Stream events: insert into session_events table, emit via Socket.IO
  4. Handle canUseTool callback for tool permissions based on session permission_mode
  5. Handle AskUserQuestion: emit session:question, wait for answer via Socket.IO
  6. On completion: update status to 'completed', set finished_at
  7. On error: update status to 'failed', store error
- Respect concurrency limits (max_concurrent_agents per project)
- Reference: playgrounds/agents/ for Agent SDK patterns

### packages/server/src/index.ts — Start the runner
- Initialize SessionRunner on server startup
- Graceful shutdown: abort running sessions on SIGTERM

### Integration with existing routes
- POST /sessions/:id/cancel: AbortController.abort() on the running session
- POST /sessions/:id/answer: Resolve pending AskUserQuestion promise
- POST /sessions/:id/permission-mode: Update canUseTool behavior

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Queued sessions automatically transition to 'running' within seconds
- [ ] Agent SDK streams events that appear in the session detail view
- [ ] Session completes and status updates to 'completed' or 'failed'
- [ ] Concurrency limits respected (no more than max_concurrent_agents running per project)
- [ ] Cancel button aborts the running agent
- [ ] Questions from agent are surfaced to the UI for user to answer

## Technical Notes
- Agent SDK: @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk query() with AbortController
- canUseTool callback MUST return { behavior: 'allow', updatedInput: input } (see CLAUDE.md)
- AskUserQuestion: hold canUseTool promise, resolve when answer arrives
- Session resume: pass resume: sessionId in options (UUID from system.init event)
- Reference implementation: playgrounds/agents/src/ — has working patterns for all of this
- This is the most critical missing piece — without it, the entire agents feature is non-functional

title: Session Resume & Control: Allow Anytime Resumption, Change Stop → Interrupt
description:
## Context

Currently, users can only interact with a session during its active turn. Once an agent completes its turn and the session goes to 'idle' state, the only way to continue is to send a message and wait for the session to resume. Additionally, the 'stop session' action likely marks the session as completed or failed, making it unresumable.

Users want:
1. Resume sessions anytime by simply sending a message (regardless of session state)
2. Change UI button from 'Stop' to 'Interrupt' — interrupts the current turn instead of terminating the session
3. Interrupted sessions should return to 'idle' state, allowing future resumption

## What to Change

**Session Resume Logic:**
- Modify session message handler to check if session is idle/completed/other terminal state
- If session has valid claude_session_id, automatically resume agent in that session (don't create new session)
- Pass message as prompt continuation: 'user says: {message}'
- Update session status from idle → running when message received

**Stop → Interrupt:**
- Rename UI button from 'Stop Session' to 'Interrupt Agent'
- Change behavior: instead of setting status='completed', trigger abortController.abort()
- Agent SDK will exit gracefully, session returns to 'idle' state (not completed/failed)
- User can resume by sending another message

**Session State Handling:**
- Idle sessions are resumable (have claude_session_id and fresh abort controller)
- Completed/failed sessions are NOT resumable (explicit user action to stop/complete)
- Distinguish between 'idle' (paused, resumable) and 'completed' (done, archived)

**Database/Schema:**
- Existing sessions.claude_session_id already supports resumption
- Existing sessions.status already has 'idle' state (resumable) vs 'completed'/'failed' (not)
- No schema changes needed; just routing/logic

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Sending a message to an idle session automatically resumes it (no explicit 'resume' button needed)
- [ ] Session resumes in same claude_session_id (chat history preserved)
- [ ] User message becomes the agent's next prompt
- [ ] UI button changed from 'Stop Session' to 'Interrupt Agent'
- [ ] Interrupt action triggers abortController.abort() (graceful exit)
- [ ] Interrupted sessions return to 'idle' state (resumable)
- [ ] Integration tests verify: idle session resumes on message, session history intact, interrupt is graceful

## Technical Notes
- Session resume already supported by agent SDK (pass 'resume' option with session ID)
- Current code has managed sessions with pendingAnswer handling for Q&A
- interrupt == abort signal; let agent SDK handle cleanup gracefully
- Completion flow: agent finishes turn → status='idle' → ready for next message
- Consider: should interrupted sessions show a "paused by user" event in the feed?
- Recommend: test interrupt behavior during active tool use (agent mid-command)

title: Implement session cost caps and tool call rate limiting
description:
## Context
No limits on token consumption or tool call frequency. A runaway agent loop can burn unlimited API tokens (denial-of-wallet) or spam destructive operations.

## What to Change

### 1. Token usage tracking (session-runner.ts)
- Add to ManagedSession: inputTokens, outputTokens, toolCallCount, toolCallTimestamps[]
- In handleMessage: extract usage from assistant.message.usage events (input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens)
- Accumulate totals per session

### 2. Cost cap enforcement
- Default limits (configurable per-project in projects table):
  - max_input_tokens: 500,000
  - max_output_tokens: 100,000
  - max_tool_calls: 200 per session
- At 80% threshold: push warning event to UI
- At 100%: abort session, push 'Session stopped: token limit reached'
- Add columns to projects table: max_session_input_tokens, max_session_output_tokens, max_session_tool_calls (nullable, use defaults if null)

### 3. Tool call rate limiting
- Track timestamps of last 60 tool calls in ManagedSession
- Calculate calls/minute using sliding window
- >30 calls/min: push warning event
- >60 calls/min: auto-pause session (set status to waiting_input with rate limit message)
- User can click 'Continue' to resume (resets window)

### 4. DB migration
- Add to projects table: max_session_input_tokens INT, max_session_output_tokens INT, max_session_tool_calls INT (all nullable)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Token usage accumulated from SDK usage events
- [ ] Warning pushed at 80% of any limit
- [ ] Session aborted at 100% of any limit
- [ ] Tool calls >60/min triggers auto-pause
- [ ] Limits configurable per-project (nullable = use defaults)
- [ ] Unit test: token accumulation and threshold detection
- [ ] Integration test: session with rate limit exceeded

## Technical Notes
- SDK usage format: message.usage = { input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens }
- Sliding window: keep array of last 60 timestamps, count within last 60 seconds
- Cost cap abort: call managed.abortController.abort()
- Depends on: ctw-12w (projects table columns for configurable limits)

## Project Context

- Debounce events (300ms) to batch rapid changes
- On change: emit Socket.IO event to project room

### 2. Socket.IO event
- Event: claude-config:changed
- Payload: { scope: 'project' | 'repo', repoId?: string, filename: string }

- **File**: packages/server/src/services/session-runner.ts

### 1. Add command policy evaluation
New private method evaluateCommandPolicy(command, managed) that:
- Loads project's command_policy from DB (cache in ManagedSession)
- Falls back to built-in defaults if null
- Returns 'block' | 'ask' | 'allow'
- Uses regex matching against pattern lists

### 2. Extend makeCanUseTool
For Bash tool: evaluate command, block or pause-and-ask
For Read tool: check against secret file deny-list, block if match
For Write/Edit tool: check if file_path is outside target_dir, pause-and-ask if so

### 3. Hard-block implementation
Return modified input that echoes a blocked message instead of executing:
{ behavior: 'allow', updatedInput: { command: 'echo "BLOCKED: ..."' } }
Push session event so UI shows what was blocked.

### 4. Pause-and-ask implementation
Reuse the existing AskUserQuestion flow:
- Update session status to waiting_input
- Push session:question event with command details
- Wait for user approval/denial via Promise
- If denied, return blocked response
- If approved, return original input

### Built-in Default Patterns
Hard-block: rm -rf /, rm -rf ~, rm -rf \$HOME, sudo, curl|bash, wget|sh, git push --force (main|master|production), shutdown, reboot, kill -9 1, docker run --privileged
Secret deny: .env*, *.pem, *.key, ~/.ssh/*, ~/.aws/*, ~/.config/gcloud/*, /proc/self/environ
Pause-ask: rm -rf, rm -r, git push, git reset --hard, git checkout ., git clean, npm publish, docker push

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Hard-blocked commands return error message to agent, never execute
- [ ] Pause-and-ask commands wait for user approval via existing Q&A UX
- [ ] Secret files cannot be read by agent
- [ ] Writes outside target_dir trigger pause-and-ask
- [ ] Session events pushed for blocked and asked commands
- [ ] Custom project patterns override defaults when set
- [ ] Unit tests for pattern matching logic
- [ ] Integration test: session with blocked command

## Technical Notes
- Reuse handleAskUserQuestion pattern for pause-and-ask (same Promise-based suspend)
- Cache project policy in ManagedSession to avoid DB lookup per tool call
- Pattern matching: simple string includes + regex for flexible patterns
- Must return { behavior: 'allow', updatedInput } per Agent SDK contract

title: Triage dialog UX: fix close icon, filter noise, add background/open-session buttons
description:
## Context
The Triage dialog (shown when clicking Triage on captures) has several UX issues: (1) Close icon styling/positioning is broken. (2) Processing phase shows noisy messages like repeated "Context: 14% used" lines — should only show meaningful progress. (3) Missing "Run in background" button to dismiss the dialog while triage continues. (4) Missing "Open session" button to navigate to the full Agent Stream page for this triage session.

## What to Change

**Close icon (packages/client/src/components/capture/triage-dialog.tsx):**
- The DialogContent from dialog.tsx already has a close button. Check if it's being obscured by the DialogHeader or ScrollArea. May need z-index or explicit positioning fix.

**Filter noisy messages (triage-dialog.tsx lines 158-165):**
- The assistantMessages filter currently shows all assistant/system events. Filter out context-percentage messages (match pattern /Context: \d+% used/). Only show messages with meaningful text content.

**Add "Run in background" button (triage-dialog.tsx processing phase ~line 259):**
- Add a button that closes the dialog without stopping the session. The session continues running. User gets a notification when complete (via existing notification system).

**Add "Open session" button (triage-dialog.tsx processing phase):**
- Add a button that navigates to /agents/sessions/{sessionId} for the full stream view. Close the dialog, mark captures as in-progress.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Close icon is visible and properly positioned in all triage dialog phases
- [ ] Processing phase only shows meaningful agent messages, not "Context: N% used" noise
- [ ] "Run in background" button available during processing phase — closes dialog, session continues
- [ ] "Open session" button available during processing phase — navigates to full agent stream page
- [ ] Background triage sends a notification when complete
- [ ] Both new buttons also available during question phase (user may want to switch to full view to answer)

## Technical Notes
- triage-dialog.tsx at packages/client/src/components/capture/triage-dialog.tsx
- sessionId is available in state once session starts (line 43) — use for Open Session link
- Filter regex for noise: /^Context: \d+(\.\d+)?% used$/
- Background: just close dialog, session keeps running via server. Socket.IO events will update session status.
- Notification: server already emits session:lifecycle events — add a toast/notification on completion
